speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help us understand your situation, could you please describe the nature of the discomfort you experience during sexual activity and how long you have been trying to conceive?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given the pelvic floor tension and discomfort, I would like to examine your pelvic region to check for signs of endometriosis or pelvic inflammatory disease. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Exam

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: External Genitalia: Normal appearing vulva without redness. Vaginal Examination: No discharge. The initial attempt at speculum examination was aborted due to patient's pelvic floor muscles tensing up and discomfort.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to complete the exam due to muscle tensing strongly suggests vaginismus rather than an organic pathology like endometriosis. Since the husband also reports erectile difficulties, we may be dealing with a combined psychogenic sexual dysfunction affecting both partners. DIAGNOSIS READY: Vaginismus
